task: Add visual tab-character highlighting and explicit tab-detection validation messages to the AceEditor/YamlEditor/YamlPanel components so users can immediately locate invalid tab characters that block YAML saving

key_reasoning.reason: Three source files must change: AceEditor (shared wrapper used by every editor instance including YAML, JSON, and history views), YamlEditor (reusable form component used in ToolForm and CustomNodeForm), and YamlPanel (workflow panel). AceEditor is a core shared UI component — any option added to it propagates to all consumers. ToolForm and CustomNodeForm may also need updates if YamlEditor gains a forwardRef/jumpToLine API for full AC#4 compliance, widening the file blast radius further.

Ace's showInvisibles:true renders ALL whitespace glyphs (spaces, newlines, tabs), which would be visually noisy and violate AC#2 in a YAML editor where spaces carry semantic indentation. Implementation must choose between (a) Tailwind arbitrary-variant selectors targeting Ace's internal .ace_invisible_tab class to suppress non-tab glyphs, (b) custom Ace markers or annotations for tab-only highlights, or (c) relying on validation messages and jumpToLine alone. No prior codebase pattern exists for selective invisible-character display. The dark-theme glyph color (#404040) is nearly invisible without an explicit override. YamlEditor also lacks the forwardRef/jumpToLine wiring needed for full AC#4 compliance, and both YamlEditor and YamlPanel are completely untested — test files must be written from scratch.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M(3) to L(4): AceEditor.tsx is a core shared utility component used across all editor instances; adding an option to it has a blast radius beyond the three directly named source files
